completion_data.completion_summary: Authored agent-system/extensions/core/context/standards/shared-worktree-discipline.md naming the read-only history-inspection techniques and the three forbidden tree-reverting git commands, registered it in index-entries.json, cross-referenced it from git-safety.md, and added a literal pointer bullet to all 15 in-scope implementation agent definitions plus the agent template. Redeployed and demonstrated the pointer chain on the deployed tree with a reproducible grep; the two Lean implementation agent definitions were deliberately left untouched per the declared scope boundary.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan's Phase 4 demonstration command assumes specific inline prose in a not-yet-written source file (e.g. a sed pattern anchored on 'Read history with'), re-derive the pattern against the actual authored content rather than running it verbatim and reporting a false negative. The plan's intent (a reproducible, cited path from a deployed agent definition to the deployed section) survives the adaptation; only the literal grep/sed anchor needs re-deriving.

Any edit to a markdown file tracked in an extension's index-entries.json (even a one-line append) immediately goes stale on that entry's declared line_count, and check-extension-docs.sh Rule R will fail doc-lint until `generate-context-line-counts.sh --write` is re-run. Budget this step after every such edit in a multi-file phase, not just once at the end -- it is cheap (reads/writes only the source index-entries.json files) and deploy-headless.sh also runs it automatically before every deploy.
